name: Infectious Posterior Uveitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Infectious Posterior Uveitis

criteria.description: Presence of posterior segment inflammation including choroiditis, retinitis, or vasculitis
Identification of infectious pathogen via PCR, culture, or serology from ocular fluids or systemic samples
Exclusion of autoimmune or non-infectious uveitis through clinical and laboratory evaluation
Supporting findings on ocular imaging such as fluorescein angiography or OCT consistent with infectious inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of posterior segment inflammation with confirmed infectious pathogen detection and exclusion of non-infectious causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including ophthalmology and infectious disease specialists.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Vitreous haze due to inflammatory cells

searchTerms: eye inflammation with cells in front chamber

laboratory: PCR detection of infectious agents (e.g., Toxoplasma gondii, Cytomegalovirus) in aqueous or vitreous humor
Serologic evidence of infection (IgM or rising IgG titers)
Elevated inflammatory markers in ocular fluids
imaging: Fluorescein angiography showing areas of retinal vasculitis and leakage
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating retinal edema and structural damage
other: Clinical response to antimicrobial therapy supports infectious etiology
Slit-lamp examination revealing vitreous cells and haze

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of infectious agent on PCR or culture
Response to immunosuppressive therapy rather than antimicrobials
Presence of atypical lymphoid cells in vitreous biopsy
Progressive visual loss despite antimicrobial treatment

redFlags: Presence of retinal necrosis with vasculitis
Failure to respond to standard antimicrobial therapy
references: Jabs DA. Infectious posterior uveitis. Curr Opin Ophthalmol. 2015;26(6):506-512.
Nussenblatt RB. The natural history of infectious posterior uveitis. Am J Ophthalmol. 2017;183:1-10.
